relationships.subject: morphine
relationships.evidence_quote: we demonstrated that sustained morphine infusion induced a significant increase in osteolysis and hypersensitivity within the ipsilateral femur through the activation of toll-like receptor-4 (TLR4)

relationships.subject: TLR4
relationships.evidence_quote: These data support TLR4, but not MOR, as necessary for morphine-induced osteolysis.

relationships.subject: TAK242
relationships.evidence_quote: This effect was completely blocked by the TLR4 antagonist, TAK242 (P < 0.0001), suggesting morphine works through a TLR4-mediated mechanism to promote osteoclastogenesis (Fig. 7B).

key_findings: Chronic morphine enhanced osteolysis and hypersensitivity in a murine breast cancer bone pain model via TLR4, not MOR.
TAK242 and TLR4 knockout ameliorated morphine-induced osteolysis and hypersensitivity.
